name: Kansas Zen Center
tradition: Zen Buddhism, Kwan Um School of Zen (Korean Seon)
about: Kansas Zen Center is a Kwan Um School of Zen (Korean Seon) practice community founded in Lawrence in 1978 by students of Zen Master Seung Sahn, now guided by Zen Master Bon Hae (Judy Roitman) and other teachers who trained on site. It owns and occupies a two-story building with an attached meditation garden, completed in 2019, where it holds weekly practice as well as a roughly monthly cycle of overnight retreats. Retreatants sleep at the center itself, typically in one large shared room (a single room is available on request), with retreat lengths ranging from a Friday-evening-to-Sunday 2-night sitting up to intensive 5- and 7-day retreats built around alternating blocks of sitting and walking meditation, chanting, 108 prostrations, and kong-an (koan) interviews with a teacher. A scheduled work period is kept in silence along with the rest of the retreat, and vegetarian meals are served temple-style during multi-day retreats. Fees are a modest set daily or per-retreat rate that is reduced or waived on request, consistent with the center's no-one-turned-away policy.
technique: Kwan Um-style Zen: sitting and walking meditation, chanting, 108 prostrations, and kong-an (koan) interviews with a teacher.
teacherAccess: Kong-an interviews with a teacher during regular practice and retreats; dharma talks and Q&A on Sundays and during retreats.
retreatOptions: One-day retreats; monthly 2-day (Friday evening-Sunday) silent retreats; periodic 5-day and 7-day intensive retreats.
schedule: Retreats run roughly monthly, from weekend 2-day sittings to week-long intensives, each with several two-hour blocks of sitting/walking meditation, chanting, and kong-an interviews with breaks for meals.
cost: Fixed per-day or per-retreat fee, reduced or waived for anyone who asks — no one is turned away for lack of funds.

pricePerDay.notes: Based on the 7-day retreat: $350 flat covers 6-7 nights (~$50/night); attending 5 or fewer nights is billed at $60/night instead.

foodNotes: Vegetarian meals are served and eaten in formal temple style during multi-day retreats; short one-day retreats are bring-your-own brown-bag lunch.
workNotes: Multi-day retreats include a scheduled work period kept in silence alongside sitting, chanting, and kong-an interviews.
